summary:
Iteration 8 (chat + promos + pricing zones + tips): Backend PASS 4/4 pytest classes (/app/backend/tests/test_extras.py, 4 tests, 10.5 s wall clock, -n 0). All spec bullets verified end-to-end against the public preview:

(1) CHAT — passenger creates a Paris→Opéra cash ride, driver (chauffeur@test.com, cleaned + online) accepts it, both parties POST /rides/{id}/messages (200), GET /messages/unread for driver returns {"unread":1} then 0 after GET /messages (mark-as-read on read side works). A freshly-registered third passenger gets 404 on /messages. After /start + /complete, POST /messages → 409 'La messagerie est disponible pendant la course uniquement'.

(2) PROMOS — moderator (passager@test.com) creates percent code (max_uses=1) 200; company (entreprise@test.com) creates amount code 200; fresh passenger /promos/validate on platform code → 200 discount=4.0, same on company code → 409 'réservé aux déplacements professionnels'; passager@test.com (member of Acme Conseil) validates existing ACME5 → 200; POST /rides with promo_code returns discount_amount>0, price=base+surcharge-discount (within 0.02 €); second /validate on max_uses=1 code → 409 'épuisé'; duplicate /promos create → 409; PATCH active=false + /validate → 404; fresh driver POST /promos → 403; DELETE by owner → 200.

(3) PRICING ZONES — GET /admin/cities as passager@test.com returns Paris; PATCH price_multiplier=1.0 → 200; POST /rides/estimate returns surcharge.price_multiplier=1.0 and standard price P1. PATCH to 1.5 → 200; estimate returns 1.5 and P2 ≈ P1 × 1.5 (diff < 0.05 €); PATCH 4.0 → 422 (Pydantic range 0.5–3.0). Paris reset to 1.0 at end of run and re-verified via API.

(4) TIPS — passenger creates card ride, driver full life-cycle, passenger /rate {rating:5, tip:3} → ride.tip=3; POST /payments/checkout/{id} {kind:'tip', return_url:https://vtc-platform-18.preview.emergentagent.com/payment-result} → 200 checkout_url starts with https://checkout.stripe.com/; GET /payments/status/{id}?kind=tip → status=pending. Additional ride rated with tip=0, tip checkout → 409 'Aucun pourboire à régler'. Verified.

FRONTEND (web 390×844) — passenger passager@test.com landing → 'Se connecter' → login form (data-testid=email-input/password-input) → home. Tapping place-1 opens the RideOptions sheet. Typing 'BIENVENUE10' in promo-input + promo-apply shows promo-applied with a green pill, price-breakdown reads 'Course 11.54 €' / 'Code BIENVENUE10 −1.15 €' / 'Total 10.39 €'. promo-remove restores the base total. Invalid code 'NOPE99' renders the API error 'invalide' in the sheet. Profil → open-promos opens promos-manager, promo-code + promo-value 15 + promo-create adds a row (verified 'UI86836' visible with -15 %, 0/utilisation(s)). open-cities-moderation opens Centres-villes with the whole city list and a search/edit UI. Verified.

Known minor UI/testID deviations from the review request wording (see action_items).
action_items: LOW (testID naming): PromosManager renders per-row `promo-active-{id}` and `promo-delete-{id}` (see /app/frontend/src/components/PromosManager.tsx:57,58). The review request asked for the generic testIDs `promo-active` / `promo-delete`. Consider aliasing the first row to the plain testIDs or update the spec — automation still passes with a prefix selector.

LOW (testID naming): CitiesModeration city rows use `city-{id}` (see /app/frontend/src/components/CitiesModeration.tsx:64). The row is a Pressable that opens the editor — tap by testID rather than by text (there is a duplicate 'Paris' string in the surcharge label on the passenger home that can confuse `get_by_text`). No functional bug.

LOW (React 19 warning, carry-over): 'Accessing element.ref was removed in React 19. ref is now a regular prop' surfaces on the login page and on the passenger home. No visible impact but keep for the next dependency sweep.
critical_code_review_comments: extras.py send_message correctly gates on ride.status ∈ (accepted, in_progress) and returns 409 otherwise — the /messages GET does the unread mark-as-read atomically via update_many. Third-party access is blocked in ride_party() before any read.

extras.py resolve_promo() enforces active + expiry + max_uses + company scope (company codes require both user.company_id==promo.company_id AND business=True) and min_price. compute_discount() clamps to [0, price] which prevents negative rides.

rides.build_ride() increments promo uses only after resolve_promo() succeeds and the ride is about to be inserted — no race but note there is no transactional guarantee: two concurrent creates on a max_uses=1 code can both slip through. Consider a $inc with a filter `uses<max_uses` (findAndModify) if this becomes a real-world concern.

geo_routes.update_city validates price_multiplier ∈ [0.5,3.0] via Pydantic (models.CityUpdateIn) — 422 works. rides.estimate applies the multiplier only to the vehicle base fare (not to surcharge), which matches the spec 'prices × multiplier'.

payments.create_checkout tip branch requires ride.tip>0 and not ride.tip_paid (409 otherwise) — passes. payment_status polling on kind=tip retrieves the Stripe session directly (no webhook secret needed for the preview) and calls mark_paid('tip') which flips ride.tip_paid + notifies the driver.
core.notify() type='message' is emitted by send_message for the counterparty — good, drives the badge count in RideChat.

PromosManager.tsx correctly hides the Alert path on web (Alert on RN Web resolves synchronously without a modal, so promo-delete confirmation dialog does not appear in Playwright — this is a well-known RN Web limitation, not a bug).

success_rate.frontend: ~90% (passenger promo apply/remove/invalid, promos-manager create, cities-moderation open all verified on web; per-row promo-active/promo-delete could not be located by the exact spec testIDs — code renders id-suffixed variants which is a naming mismatch, not a functional bug; rating-with-tip + in-ride chat UI + company promo creation were left to main-agent self-verification since they are already covered end-to-end by pytest and the underlying flows are the same code paths as iteration-7)

seed_data_creation: Created throwaway users: TEST_passenger_* and TEST_driver_* via /api/auth/register for the third-party 404, non-privileged 403 and fresh-passenger company-scope assertions. Created and deleted promo codes PLAT*/COMP*/TOGL* during the run, and the UI-created promo 'UI86836' was cleaned up post-run. Paris price_multiplier restored to 1.0 (verified via GET /admin/cities). No touch to chauffeur@test.com or entreprise@test.com beyond one card ride each (rated, so no active state left).
context_for_next_testing_agent: pytest suite /app/backend/tests/test_extras.py is idempotent (fresh registrations + unique promo suffixes each run) — always run with `pytest backend/tests/test_extras.py -n 0` (module-scoped fixtures share the driver_mod_tok that goes online at startup and clears any leftover active rides). The chat 409-after-complete assertion depends on the ride being completed inside the test; if the driver has a leftover in_progress ride from a previous crash, the fixture's _cleanup_active() will complete it — but if the driver had an 'accepted' ride pending it will be cancelled (safe). Frontend flows still awaiting UI coverage: (a) driver-home open-chat button after accepting a passenger ride, (b) passenger rating-box with tip-2 + submit-rating showing 'Envoyer et donner 2.00 €', (c) company entreprise@test.com → Entreprise tab → open-promos → create employee code (identical component, subtitle changes to 'Codes promo employés'). All three code paths are trivial and their backend counterparts are covered by pytest — recommend main agent self-verify visually.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no functional bugs surfaced in this iteration. Two initial Playwright script bumps were purely test-authoring: (i) the app landing page shows a 'Se connecter' button that navigates to the login form (I initially expected the login form to be the entry screen) — fixed by clicking 'Se connecter' first, then filling email-input/password-input; (ii) tapping city 'Paris' via get_by_text picked up the 'Paris – centre-ville' surcharge label on the passenger home instead of the city row in the moderation sheet — non-issue, the sheet renders correctly with city-{id} testIDs.
